claims.text: Machine-learning refinement of EAM potentials will improve representation of atomic configurations in ab initio liquid high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states.
EAM potentials can be refined using machine learning.
The intervention is intended for high-entropy alloys near their high melting temperatures and in near-liquid states.
Machine-learning algorithms can adapt EAM potentials using training data from ab initio calculations.
Training on a diverse set of atomic configurations will enable the model to represent the complex phase space of high-entropy alloys better.
Machine-learning-refined EAM potentials will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to traditional EAM references.
Machine-learning-refined EAM potentials will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to traditional EAM references.
Current EAM references do not adequately represent liquid-state configurations.
The method is applicable to high-entropy alloys with known elemental compositions.
The method is applicable at temperatures approaching the alloys' melting points.
Effectiveness in capturing high-entropy-alloy configurational complexity cannot be established without empirical validation.
Refined machine-learning EAM and traditional EAM references should be compared on the same high-entropy-alloy system at high temperature.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement in free-energy predictions and phase stability would falsify the hypothesis.
